tiers.name: Amyl Rachis
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: One of seven strangers who woke on the road with their years missing. Steady-handed and quiet-spoken; the company's patience, and often its conscience.

tiers.name: Amyl Rachis
tiers.label: keeper of the Rot Door
tiers.text: The trial under the bough was his: a burden of loneliness, carried willingly rather than suffered. What he keeps, he keeps by choice, and it has begun to answer to him.

tiers.name: Amyl Rachis
tiers.label: who says the names
tiers.text: He keeps the names of the taken the way other men keep coin — the cobbler's first among them — and says them at need, like a man saluting. In the intake hall he claimed a boy from a city's paperwork with one sentence.

tiers.name: Tirig
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: A huntress of the North, reader of ground and weather. She counts exits before she counts friends, and is rarely wrong about either.

tiers.name: Tirig
tiers.label: keeper of the Winter Door
tiers.text: Her trial was the white forest: a lifetime's melancholy met in deep snow, and not denied — I left; there is a difference; and I am exactly where I was going. The amulet is returned to its socket under the two skies, and the singing it pointed to has come closer: behind her sternum now, patient as a second pulse.

tiers.name: Tirig
tiers.label: whom the crystal sings to
tiers.text: The amulet called the Heart of Winter's Veil answers her as an instrument answers its player. At the Mooring of Ascore, needles swung when she passed. She has begun wondering a thing she does not say aloud.

tiers.name: Tirig
tiers.label: the suspicion
tiers.text: In the receiving hall she heard a sentence shaped like one from the silent films, on the lips of a small gray-eyed woman, and a suspicion entered her that has not left.
tiers.todo: Higher tiers (what she truly carries; the keeper's ending) unlock in unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: Corvyn
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: A stonemason's son with a musician's ear. He cannot read a room of powerful people, and can read anything with staves on it.

tiers.name: Corvyn
tiers.label: keeper of the Stone Door
tiers.text: His trial was the bought glade: a lifetime's debt met at its source, and found to be misfiled — the craft was bought; the music was always his. He stands surety now for the fairy who bought his life, plays first for the Winter Court in perpetuity, and carries a folded contract toward a very particular fire.

tiers.name: Corvyn
tiers.label: who hums at old doors
tiers.text: He carries three wrong notes the way other men carry keys, and the elder work answers them. A bottle bought back from a collector rides in his pack, wrapped, unopened, shining.

tiers.name: Corvyn
tiers.label: who read the butcher's diagram
tiers.text: In the workroom under Fundament he read the tune taken apart — every phrase inverted, every resolution refused — and named it for the company: somebody took the kindest thing he knows and arranged it to cut.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: A horned soldier of iron discipline and banked heat. He speaks of a paladin's order and keeps a soldier's table; his brothers are often in his mouth and never at his side.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: keeper of the Ember Door
tiers.text: His trial was the barrow: fifteen years of wrath, met cold. The massacre that made him was staged — his family tinder for a warlock escort's disappearance — and offered the kill that would settle every ledger on schedule, he looked at the emptied man instead and said: I am owed a debt. Not by you. Collect it yourself.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: the enforcer
tiers.text: The order was never a paladin's. His strength was purchased, his service engineered, and the patron who holds his paper has a name the company first heard smiling at a masquerade.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: the asset, at dinner
tiers.text: In the Hells he sat at his owner's table and learned the terms of an old paper read aloud: thirteen days owned, and the rest of him inventoried. He answered with the only defiance a man in a contract has — his brothers kept a better table in a tent in the rain.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: who took his own mouth back
tiers.text: In the fire of an estate that is its owner, he tore a letter free, understood the way a falling man understands the ground, and said the name syllable by syllable. The compulsion cracked. The purchase burned. The calling — the oath, the tent-and-rain words — was never for sale.

tiers.name: Iratius
tiers.label: unpurchased
tiers.text: His strength was never his — the patron's grace, poured year over year into a man who knelt at every dawn and thought he knew who was listening. Revoked in a doorway with a snap, having cost its giver nothing to take. He said the oath anyway, all of it, slowly — to no one, and to whoever is actually there.
tiers.todo: The Tyr grant unlocks in unwritten chapter XLIII.

tiers.name: Saeron Redcord
tiers.label: kitchen chef of the Boar's Rest
tiers.text: A monk of the Broken God, met over a stove. Hands that feed people and remember other work; an old arrangement with the worst duty in any room.

tiers.name: Saeron Redcord
tiers.label: the Iriaebor survivor
tiers.text: The folded page, unfolded at last against a prepared town, matched it like a stencil. He has seen this play before: Iriaebor — the quarter he grew up in, emptied on a festival night nine years ago, and the world agreed to call it a plague. He knows the curtain is not yet up.

tiers.name: Saeron Redcord
tiers.label: keeper of the cord
tiers.text: His trial was the Feast of the Moon: an empathy thrown wide open by its own kin, wanting him to carry every need in the room until he died of being needed. He did the opposite of everything — he delegated, name by name, round by round, spending his friends like a man who has finally accepted the truth he once gave a dying warden: the rope holds because it is a rope, and not because one knot carries the line.

tiers.name: Saeron Redcord
tiers.label: who empties the column
tiers.text: He carries an iron key over his heart and a mason's name in his ledger — Bettany's husband, nine years in transit, recoverable pending capacity. He has stated his intention plainly: we are emptying that column.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: A dry-voiced skeptic with uncanny gray-touched features nobody can quite place, least of all him. He keeps the company's ledgers of doubt, and a shield blazoned with scales.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: keeper of the Grave Door
tiers.text: His trial was the first and the strangest: an ambivalence so total it must choose nothing — unchosen, and made to choose aloud. He said the Queen's words, because her rite keeps and his life was made of unclosed doors. And the throne of bone is told to the company at last: not a nightmare; a schedule, with more than one party keeping it.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: the taken
tiers.text: A shard the length of a boar-spear, aimed by a dying mirror's whole attention — and he had finished, forever, with stepping aside. It was easy, he told them, surprised, and pleased, and younger than any of them had ever heard him. Taken whole into the country the feathers came from, under a fall of black like weather escaping its frame, leaving Bayne laid straight on the stones for other people to find.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: the retrieved
tiers.text: Found standing at a pane in the collector's house, days deep in a vigil for a sleeping man he cannot name — the shape of what was taken from him, asleep, with its arm around where he goes. Retrieved by his friends, his wound closed with a seam of pale glass. Not healed: held. He is alive, and his death is also alive, and they are wearing the same body.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: half of the gray country
tiers.text: The uncanny in his face has a name now: Shadar-kai blood, unknown to him his whole life. His father serves at a table the company has stood before, and knew him on sight.

tiers.name: Sov Thimron
tiers.label: the consideration clause
tiers.text: On a rampart of Fundament his father gave him the terms: his mother was Lenore of Ormath; the bargain that made him has a clause, and he is it. His father has kept a dead woman's bargain for thirty years and invites him to read the terms himself.

tiers.name: Aelendir Springwhisper
tiers.label: of the company of seven
tiers.text: One of the seven, though he came to the circle last of them — an ancient Eladrin of the College of Glamour, courteous and evasive in equal measure, whose instrument is a bowl of resonant metal. His centuries do not add up, and he knows it; when the gray took the masked hall, he stood inside the circle as though it had been waiting for him.

tiers.name: Aelendir Springwhisper
tiers.label: in whom a bowl was struck
tiers.text: At Triboar a dissonance rang in him like a struck instrument, and has not stopped. There are years in him that are simply gone — not forgotten; removed — and the tune he shares with the company troubles him like a face at a window.

tiers.name: Aelendir Springwhisper
tiers.label: clerk of the names
tiers.text: He confirms names at intake stations and enters losses in a precise clerk's hand, because names are his oldest business, and making a written line true is the only mending he can always do.

tiers.name: Aelendir Springwhisper
tiers.label: who found his own hand
tiers.text: In the enemy's workroom he lifted a conserved sheet four centuries old and read his own notation: the tune, entire, set down whole for a commission he is only beginning to remember. There was a fellowship. There was a wall. There was a woman, and he knew her name, and the name will not cross his tongue — not lost; held.
tiers.todo: Tier 5 (the Remembrance; what he was there for) unlocks at door07's Remembrance and unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: Aelendir Springwhisper
tiers.label: there at the beginning
tiers.todo: Tier 5 (the Spring Door proper; his Malethymia — Intrigue or Nostalgia, still an open ruling) unlocks at door07's unwritten chapter.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: a boy of Triboar
tiers.text: A tiefling boy of Triboar, carried alive and impossibly cold out of the dark beneath Ransor's Open Road. Small, watchful, and quicker to recover than anyone had a right to expect.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: the smallest ambassador
tiers.text: In the socket of pale light at the harnessed thing's heart, barefoot and calm, he relayed three truths in both directions and talked a mountain down — then sat on the stone and cried like the child he had never quite been allowed to be. Carried out asleep. The first person the party ever saved, saved twice.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: kept at Moongleam
tiers.text: The Harpers gave him a small room with a west window, and he stayed while the staying was good. He hears what no one else hears, and Moongleam's hum — he insists — is wrong.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: who would not be kept
tiers.text: The calling turned — a stream become a going-away — and he left with two good cloaks toward Silverymoon, and east of it every line that watched him went blind. The quiet thing was moving. He followed it.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: the one awake arrival
tiers.text: He came through the Crossing on his own feet with his eyes open — the thing the whole tender apparatus exists to make impossible — said four words to the seven, and went down like a tide going out.

tiers.name: Gregory
tiers.label: the river-shaped boy
tiers.text: A year of the link ran through him like a river through a valley, and the valley is the shape of the river now. He answers thoughts spoken too loudly, knows things that surface when the ground of talk passes over them, and speaks for something that has few ways left to say anything. He is one of them.

tiers.name: The Archivist
tiers.label: a clerk of Fundament
tiers.text: A small gray-eyed woman who meets arrivals with a folder and a filed, efficient kindness. The name, she says, comes with the office; the rest of hers would only clutter your first day.

tiers.name: The Archivist
tiers.label: who runs the floor
tiers.text: At intake she spends kindness at scale — rehearsed love, love drilled like a fire brigade — checking blanket-weight against crossing-chill with her own cheek. Whatever else is true in that hall, her tenderness is not a performance. That is going to be the problem.

tiers.name: The Archivist
tiers.label: the suspicion
tiers.text: She said a sentence shaped exactly like one the gray country spent a year showing them, and an old elf half-knows her face and cannot find the shelf it is on. Whether she is the woman he cannot name, or someone that woman kept, or both, or neither — nobody has said aloud.

tiers.name: The Archivist
tiers.label: who did not ask one question
tiers.text: When a boy arrived awake — the one thing her apparatus exists to prevent — something older looked out through the gray for three heartbeats, and then she filed him under the household of the seven without a single question. A Lord Protector stepped bodily into that look, and would do it again.
tiers.todo: Tiers 5–6 (who she is; what she was to the ring; what she does with the song) unlock at door07 and unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: The Girl in the Gray
tiers.label: a figure in the dream's color
tiers.text: A girl glimpsed in the dream's impossible color, grieving at a grave beneath a great tree. Words do not reach her and hands pass through her; whatever she is, the mourning is real, and the dream is patient with her, as though she matters more than the dreamers.

tiers.name: The Girl at the Grave
tiers.label: the refused name
tiers.text: The name on her grave-stone is plain, whole, and unreadable — it slides out of perception the instant it is grasped, refused the mind like two like poles of a lodestone. Someone, or something, has seen to it that this name cannot be known.

tiers.name: The Girl at the Grave
tiers.label: who kept what she loved
tiers.text: The films assemble a life: a mother buried under a great tree, a grief kept in worked stone, a gift for holding what others let go. The Remembrances play her without sound, and the fidelity of each scene is exactly the attention she paid it.

tiers.name: The Girl at the Grave
tiers.label: who paid herself away
tiers.text: Piece by piece — a vow, a rope in a blizzard, a letting-go — she traded her own keeping for other people's. What the company carries under their names are shards of what she felt. They are what she kept.

tiers.name: The Girl at the Grave
tiers.label: whose name is kept
tiers.text: Her name has been struck from history — not lost; held, like a word on the far side of glass. This codex cannot record it. Someone in Fundament has her song, and has been taking it apart.
tiers.todo: Tiers 6+ (the stone; the two skies; what she became) unlock at door07 and unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: Darathra Shendrel
tiers.label: Lord Protector of Triboar
tiers.text: The soldier who runs Triboar: musters honest, ledgers square, door oiled. Forty years of close things and a shield-wall behind her; her town trusts her the way a roof is trusted.

tiers.name: Darathra Shendrel
tiers.label: who went where her town went
tiers.text: On the night of the Harvest she marshaled the stair and counted the rescued through the arch in tens; wrote on her own forearm at the arch's head, unhurried as a woman labeling a crate; said A Lord Protector goes where her town goes; and went down her own stair into the rising glass, like a woman going down to answer her own door.

tiers.name: Darathra Shendrel
tiers.label: ward-captain of Fundament
tiers.text: Alive, whole, and running housing wards in the city of the saved — with no memory of her crossing night, and a two-finger watch-sign for those she once commanded. She mourned seven people and is extremely angry it was wasted.

tiers.name: Darathra Shendrel
tiers.label: who read her own hand
tiers.text: A transcription of her forearm was recited back to her by seven witnesses: her private death-rite, written only when death stands certain in the doorway. Either the page lies — and it is her hand — or everything this city told her about that night is a lie built exactly the size of her death. They stole her consent. That is the crime. Not the taking. The forgetting.

tiers.name: Darathra Shendrel
tiers.label: who fills in the blanks
tiers.text: She pulled the advance lists, found the undated names, and stood in the intake hall writing the hour in the margin — filling in the one blank the enemy's paperwork left her. She kept her promise. She intends to remember keeping it.

tiers.name: Merris Thulane
tiers.label: Inquisitor of the Twelve
tiers.text: Keeper of audits and lower levels in Triboar's Tower; a name spoken with respect and a face nobody sees. When the alarm went up, she went down, and did not come back.

tiers.name: Merris Thulane
tiers.label: the traitor at the table
tiers.text: The sluice was never forced. She burned the records rather than let a tampering be read, opened the Twelve's forgotten door, and went down through it ahead of the raiders she let in — toward whatever she serves, leaving a silenced witness and a betrayed old woman holding a key-ring in a smoking room.

tiers.name: Merris Thulane
tiers.label: the willing
tiers.text: At the turn of the last battle she stepped backward into the rising glass — not defiance, not fear: relief. It closed over her smiling. Not the kind of believer who fights to the last; a fanatic choosing her own altar. That, at least, is what it looked like.

tiers.name: Merris Thulane
tiers.label: where betrayal retires to
tiers.text: She works intake now, gray still, sash gone, stylus ticking down her columns — the first willing traveler, entirely at home. You made good time, she told the seven. Welcome to the work. She meant every word.

tiers.name: Veyran
tiers.label: the sommelier
tiers.text: The masquerade's bartender — perfect poise, a fraction too much sharpness in the smile, the kind of man you remember for reasons you can't quite name. There is something behind the smile that does not match the apron.

tiers.name: Veyran
tiers.label: who casts no shadow
tiers.text: The lamplight falls on him and stops. A tossed coin passes through him. He remembers a desperate paladin's assurances, names Volcaris as lightly as a garnish, disclaims the party's bond while confirming it — the knot that binds you was tied with defter hands than mine — and has declared himself, smiling, an enemy.

tiers.name: Veyran
tiers.label: the efficient devil
tiers.text: A devil, named at blade-length by the man he emptied. He engineered a false massacre fifteen years deep — a warlock escort buying its freedom with a stolen soul in a lead box, a family spent as tinder — and he staffs his web with brokers and pleasant men at parties, people who owe him, paid in exactly the coin they dream in. Never a generous devil. An efficient one.

tiers.name: Xantraxis
tiers.label: the collector, at home
tiers.text: In the Hells he keeps an estate that is himself, a wine-wall of vintages that are not wine, and a table at which he dines alone before his assets. Waste, he says, is the only sin he recognizes.

tiers.name: Xantraxis
tiers.label: the patron
tiers.text: The gentleman's true name, and the fiend behind two bindings the company has met: a warlock's paper and a squire's geas. He engineers debts the way masons lay courses, and declares his enmities politely.

tiers.name: Xantraxis
tiers.label: the yielding
tiers.text: His conversion of a claim was ruled appetite before nine witnesses and his own display; the pact burned entire on a very particular fire, and notice of its destruction will be served wherever appetite winters now. He yielded to a clerk, not to a sword, and he loves that about the world exactly as much as he says.
tiers.todo: Tier 6 (the Avernus party at the Ascension) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLIII.

tiers.name: The Raven Queen
tiers.label: of the gray country
tiers.text: The power that keeps the Shadowfell's roads and the dead's crossings: named in field prayers, blamed in doctrines, described by no reliable witness. Her servants wear sorrow like livery.

tiers.name: The Raven Queen
tiers.label: who keeps
tiers.text: The Lady who keeps what is lost. Her rite does not close; it keeps. A seep silvered over at her words in a Silverymoon crypt, and somewhere in her country there are shelves of glass, cold as libraries, quiet as vaults — and on them, sleepers. Kept whole. Kept still. Kept.

tiers.name: The Raven Queen
tiers.label: the collection, complete
tiers.text: The courtship, answered — or claimed. When the shard let Sov Thimron go, the feathers came down like a film's weather escaping its frame, and the room held a folded, vast patience that no account agrees on. What it left behind: Bayne, laid straight, exactly the way feathers had been laid for him on sills and snow-crusts the whole length of the book.

tiers.name: The Raven Queen
tiers.label: her one appearance
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (her one appearance) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLV.

tiers.name: Hyuth Kolstaag
tiers.label: seller of assurances
tiers.text: A wealthy, difficult man of Triboar — host of the Boar's Rest masquerade, seller of 'assurances' to the rich and the frightened, guarded by better arms than the town can field. His toast quotes words he does not seem to know he is quoting.

tiers.name: Hyuth Kolstaag
tiers.label: the bound tongue
tiers.text: His silences were never all his: a compulsion, fiend-work, that seizes his throat at the approach of certain matters. He delayed the party under orders he could not name, and engineered a doomed love without being allowed to keep the reason.

tiers.name: Hyuth Kolstaag
tiers.label: in Harper keeping
tiers.text: He shelters at Moongleam under the Harpers' wardship, unbound a little more each season, learning what his family's debts actually purchased.

tiers.name: Aevren
tiers.label: a veiled courier
tiers.text: A Harper who moves letters and people through the North under a veil, and offers to decode what others cannot read. No one knows where she sleeps.

tiers.name: Aevren
tiers.label: keys and whiles
tiers.text: Keys she had; whiles she made. The decode came north by indignant bird: the Ledger opened, the calendar read, and a warning attached in her careful hand — do not speak the vain name aloud until we know its weight.

tiers.name: Aevren
tiers.label: the household note
tiers.text: Because you will want it and will not ask: the boy would not be kept. He said the quiet thing was moving, and said it the way weather says things. Walked to Silverymoon under two good cloaks; east of it, her lines lost him. I am not, in truth, certain sorry is the right entry.

tiers.name: Mishka
tiers.label: keeper of the Northshield
tiers.text: The keeper of the Northshield Inn — half-orc shoulders, a veteran's eye, and a floor she does not permit blood on. Half the room fears her; the other half merely respects her, which suits her fine.

tiers.name: Mishka
tiers.label: the saved
tiers.text: She woke on a quay in Fundament with a blanket on her and a stranger saying saved, and no memory of the night between. She said seven names into a basin and paid for the candles. She does not pick at the seams of it. Most days.

tiers.name: Gorvach
tiers.label: the frost-bound
tiers.text: An orc of the Veilmark Clan who walked out of the north unarmed and half-frozen, taken without a struggle by a patrol he did not resist. Frost no season explains; veins pale with a shimmer like starlight; a geas that owns his whys. Sent to find something that is no longer in the North — something now in mortal hands — from a white forest with two skies.

tiers.name: Gorvach
tiers.label: keeper of the mouth
tiers.text: Free now, in furs instead of chains, he keeps the breathing cave of the Veilmark — for the ones who kept him. He stands in its cold exhalation as other men stand in sunlight, gives the mouth's one law — inside, do not take; it counts — and bows to the crystal, not its bearer.

tiers.name: Gorvach
tiers.label: the second word
tiers.text: At the wool-house stair, in the full morning light, in the letters a monk taught him on a shield-face, his second word stands carved for Nesmé to puzzle over for a generation: KEEP.
tiers.todo: Tier 4 (the Kept Gate; the knife handed back) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLIV.

tiers.name: Gurpnik
tiers.label: of the Twelve's service
tiers.text: A stern-eyed dwarf in the service of the Twelve — Nik, to those who know him — who found a stranger collapsed at Gwaeron's Rest with no wound and no struggle, and carried her to warmth. The town needs hands; he offers his.

tiers.name: Nik
tiers.label: who would not leave her twice
tiers.text: At the graveyard wall, with the yard's yews already entombed, he said something with twice in it, and went over the wall into the glass-light with his axe in his hand — a dwarf walking into the end of the world to stand over his wife's memorial. The party did not see him taken. They chose, forever after, to believe that mattered.

tiers.name: Nik
tiers.label: keeper of a wall
tiers.text: In Fundament he keeps a wall and a shrine-shelf of doctrine he does not entirely believe. He remembers more than he says at the shrine — and he has said so to exactly one person.

tiers.name: Sera
tiers.label: of the Twelve, and missing
tiers.text: One of the Twelve who keep Triboar, and the reason the party walked the tree-line of Gwaeron's Rest: she went into the western wood and did not come back. The search goes out with more fear in it than anyone will name.

tiers.name: Sera
tiers.label: what the wood gave back
tiers.text: Found at the edge of a ransacked camp, half-hidden beneath a bush, with the wood already taking her in. Not merely killed — killed with intention, in a manner Sov knew at once for ritual: some working, for which her death was the instrument. Clutched in her hand, a torn pendant bearing the mark of Shar and a second sign belonging to no faith he could name; scattered behind her, the numbered letters of a secret love. She was Nik's wife.

tiers.name: Sera
tiers.label: the silver in her
tiers.text: The mirror showed her truth through her husband's memory: silver threads, a glow like the moon within her veins, a light not wholly hers to give — why the ground where she died grows lush where all else withers, and why her death was purpose, not only loss. Her dried blood burns argent, and darkness recoils from it.

tiers.name: Sera
tiers.label: whose protection was altered
tiers.text: Someone tampered with the Twelve's rotations in the days before she walked into the wood alone, and an inquisitor burned the records rather than let the tampering be read. Her love itself was engineered — the meeting, the letters, the whole doomed romance — on instructions its arranger cannot name.

tiers.name: Sera
tiers.label: Alustriel's daughter
tiers.text: She was Alustriel Silverhand's daughter — one of many, and every one of them carries the Silver Fire whether they will or no. She spent all of hers in one breath, untrained, unasked, to spoil a working she could not have named. Killed not for what she knew — for what her blood could close. Murdered by planners, for a door she never knew she was.

tiers.name: Darz Helgar
tiers.label: the truest mourner
tiers.text: Triboar's groundskeeper — a heavyset laborer with dirt-seamed hands and a grief too large to hide, who loved in secret and now has nowhere to put the loss. Almost certainly D. Almost certainly harmless.

tiers.name: Darz Helgar
tiers.label: the ignorant instrument
tiers.text: He played his bar of the score on cue, on instructions he could not name, steered by a friendship that was never a friendship. What used him is accounted elsewhere in this codex.

tiers.name: Darz Helgar
tiers.label: winter's arrangement
tiers.text: He walked north through the autumn and came changed: bare hands unremarked in the sleet, a gray cast at the rim of each iris, a steadiness one degree off level. Winter and I came to an arrangement is every answer anyone got. And an ache in his teeth now maps what the quiet towns are curing — worst of all along one blind brick wall in Nesmé.

tiers.name: Bettany & Osric
tiers.label: the monk and the witness
tiers.text: Osric — Saeron's kin in the stern, kind way of their order, six winters tracing a pattern of festival-night disappearances up the river-roads with prayers and paperwork. And Bettany — a witness of the night Iriaebor's quarter burned, who has spent nine years trying to decide what she saw a man do on the barracks stair.

tiers.name: Bettany & Osric
tiers.label: pending capacity
tiers.text: The waiting has a ledger line now: a mason's name, nine years in transit, recoverable pending capacity. The company has stated its intention about that column.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the recovery) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLIV.

tiers.name: Alustriel Silverhand
tiers.label: the beloved absent
tiers.text: High Lady of Silverymoon for centuries, and famously gone — her name said over every second shop-door in the tone reserved for beloved absent things, and heard once already through a mask at Boar's Rest.

tiers.name: Alustriel Silverhand
tiers.label: who gave two memories back
tiers.text: Her Silver Fire closed the crossing under the Tree and healed it at the root; and at a small fire apart she lent the Tree a voice — ten heartbeats of true remembering: the gray is a place, a shore the seven have stood on together since before any of them could hold a spoon. And to one of the company she gave back a night: rain, grave-soil, a working answered from below.

tiers.name: The Guide
tiers.label: a gray companion of the roads
tiers.text: A Shadar-kai who walks the gray country like a man consulting a clock he already trusts, and delivers the company where they are expected.

tiers.name: Insight
tiers.label: Oracle of Truth
tiers.text: His chair at the Session handles what is coming, and his vote is spoken for it. He rose, faced the gallery, and inclined his head once. Like a colleague.

tiers.name: Insight
tiers.label: the father, the note payable
tiers.text: He is Sov's father, and says so on a rampart without ceremony. The seam, he teaches, is a note payable: she does not call her notes early; she waits to be asked. The asking is coming. He has spoken for it in session.

tiers.name: Verity
tiers.label: the firm, unhurried hand
tiers.text: Prepare for Harvest. The field is gathered. There you are. Signed always in full — a title is a promise; an initial is an escape hatch. At a council table in a doubled-light city, the Enforcer reports defeats the way defeats ought to be reported: dates, numbers, no adjectives.

tiers.name: Verity
tiers.label: the one who does not believe it
tiers.text: The hand that laid Nesmé's tables and wrote There you are — Saeron knows her squared corners by candlelight. And when a clerk let slip a certain reversal in a certain demesne, her eyes came up from her papers to the gallery for half a second, and nothing in her face moved at all. At least one person at that table does not believe the story.

tiers.name: Clarity
tiers.label: of the legation
tiers.text: Of the Fundament legation in Silverymoon — a tiefling woman of middle years, horns ringed in plain silver, dressed with the restraint that costs the most, making councilors taller by laughing. The party had seen her word once before, at the bottom of nothing; it is one thing to know your enemy has signatures, and another to watch one stand up, smooth her coat, and walk.

tiers.name: Clarity
tiers.label: Diplomat of Truth
tiers.text: The caller's virtue was not an affectation. It was a title. Her office handles what is outside, and her sincerity is not softened by the office one degree. She means every word of it.

tiers.name: Certitude
tiers.label: Priest of Truth
tiers.text: An aasimar cleric of the Consensus whose office handles what is kept. He touches a reliquary when doctrine is questioned, which is often.

tiers.name: Certitude
tiers.label: who bows to an empty chair
tiers.text: Believing himself unwatched, he bows to the seventh chair at the table's head. His questions have a single answer. Nobody weeps over saved, he says, and believes it is mercy.

tiers.name: Conviction
tiers.label: Warrior of Truth
tiers.text: A dwarf fighter of the Consensus whose office handles what is far. He comes to table travel-stained, with the North still on his boots, and puts his helmet down like a deadline.

tiers.name: Conviction
tiers.label: the deadline
tiers.text: He argues logistics the way soldiers argue weather — as a thing to be survived, not persuaded. Say saved and be done; nobody weeps over saved. Which way he breaks when the table breaks is not yet written in any ledger.
tiers.todo: Her side in the split is an open ruling; resolves in unwritten chapter XLIII.

tiers.name: Revelation
tiers.label: Seeker of Truth
tiers.text: A half-elf wizard, thin as a bookmark, whose office handles what is unknown. The numbers go to him, and he follows them wherever they walk.

tiers.name: Edda Vell
tiers.label: warden of the Tower
tiers.text: Keeper of Triboar Tower's keys and rotations, who took one look at the burned cabinets and went very still. She died at her own door, keys spilling like a chime.

tiers.name: The Sleeper
tiers.label: kept, with his arm around an absence
tiers.text: A young man asleep behind glass: wheat-and-copper hair, a fair face freckled by outdoor summers, mason's linen wraps gone soft with washing, a leather apron still on — sleep taken between one task and the next, a small round medal polished by a thumb's worrying. One arm lies curved on the empty air beside him, holding its shape around an absence exactly the size of someone.

tiers.name: Torrin
tiers.label: the name
tiers.todo: Tier 2 (the name; the asking) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIV–XLV.

tiers.name: The Presence Below
tiers.label: a fear beneath the town
tiers.text: Something vast lies under Triboar — old enough to frighten vermin into carpets, near enough to feel like a heartbeat under the floor. It is not hunting. It is afraid, and it noticed the two who could hear it.

tiers.name: The Presence Below
tiers.label: readied
tiers.text: Whatever it is, it is being readied — down there, beneath the festival, by hands that keep a calendar. Its dread has a direction now, and the direction is up.

tiers.name: The Gravemind
tiers.label: the harnessed
tiers.text: Its name, when the record finally yields it: the Gravemind. A vast slow mass of once-things — root and antler, rats and men — held in a third state between life and death, harnessed by couplings of black glass as the engine of the working. Talked down by three truths passed through the smallest ambassador in the history of embassies, it let go: not free, not whole, no longer entirely harnessed.

tiers.name: The Quiet Thing
tiers.label: the big quiet thing
tiers.text: A boy gives it its gentler name: the quiet thing. It holds him gently, and he alone can hear it; when it was moved, he would not be kept, and followed.

tiers.name: The Engine
tiers.label: harnessed again
tiers.text: It has been made into an engine after all — moved slowly, at night, in pieces of attention, and used. It doesn't want to be an engine. Nobody asked it. Nobody has ever asked it anything.
tiers.todo: Tier 6 (what it is; what cuts it free) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLIII.

tiers.name: Triboar
tiers.label: a crossroads town of the North
tiers.text: Three roads, an honest muster, a masked festival coming, and a Lord Protector who keeps it all square. The kind of town wars are fought to get back to.

tiers.name: Triboar
tiers.label: the readied town
tiers.text: Beneath the festival, a score was being played: audits, rotations, a presence under the graveyard, and an order signed by a virtue. Prepare for Harvest.

tiers.name: Triboar
tiers.label: the taken
tiers.text: The town fell in one night of rising glass — taken whole, standing, held like flies in amber, while a stag the size of a house shepherded the runners west. What remains east of the crossroads is a ruin that still smells faintly of festival.

tiers.name: The Boar's Rest
tiers.label: Hyuth Kolstaag's manor
tiers.text: Hyuth Kolstaag's manor outside Triboar — a great hall fit for a masquerade, private guards better armed than anything the town can field, and a cellar the invitations do not mention.

tiers.name: The Boar's Rest
tiers.label: the masquerade's stage
tiers.text: The festival's masks came here, and so did guests who were not what their masks said. Some of what happened under its lanterns proved, afterward, to be mostly illusion.

tiers.name: The Lord Protector's Tower
tiers.label: Triboar's keep
tiers.text: Darathra's seat: musters, records, the Twelve's rotations, and — at its head — an arch that is more than architecture.

tiers.name: The Lord Protector's Tower
tiers.label: the last stair
tiers.text: On the night of the Harvest its arch took the rescued in counted tens; its warden died at its door with her keys spilling down the steps like a chime; and its lady wrote on her own arm at the arch's head before going back down her own stairs.

tiers.name: Moongleam Tower
tiers.label: a Harper hold in Everlund
tiers.text: A tower of the Harpers with a translocation arch and a habit of taking in what the roads wash up.

tiers.name: Moongleam Tower
tiers.label: where the forty landed
tiers.text: The arch received Triboar's evacuated children and their minders on the night the town fell. A boy with a west-window room stayed there a while, and its hum — one guest insists — is wrong.

tiers.name: Silverymoon
tiers.label: the Gem of the North
tiers.text: The North's city of bridges and colleges, silver-lit, where the company is received at a level they did not ask for.

tiers.name: Silverymoon
tiers.label: the escalation's middle rung
tiers.text: What burned at a cave and again at Triboar pressed here third — and was answered by Silver Fire. Even gems, it transpires, are being counted by someone.

tiers.name: The Grandfather Tree
tiers.label: an elder of the High Forest
tiers.text: The oldest living thing on any map the Harpers keep — a tree like a hill with a canopy like a county, mother-grove to every circle of the North, far west in the deeps of the High Forest. Beneath its boughs the seniors of the circles are assembling, and asking hard questions.

tiers.name: The Grandfather Tree
tiers.label: the pried grip
tiers.text: The Tree holds a door shut — it is what the oldest living things are for — and a pin of black glass seated in its heartwood with a jeweler's care is prying that grip loose, vein by tallied vein, logged by the tenday and signed with a title for a name.

tiers.name: The Grandfather Tree
tiers.label: healed at the root
tiers.text: The rot's cause was bought and paid for elsewhere; its cure cost the company a trial under the boughs and ended in Silver Fire and two restored memories.

tiers.name: Nesmé
tiers.label: a walled town on the Evermoors' edge
tiers.text: A stubborn ring of walls on the Evermoors' edge, buying blade-coin against the winter the way moor towns do when the year turns.

tiers.name: Nesmé
tiers.label: the town that stood
tiers.text: The first one. The mirror in shards, the working dead ahead of its hour, and twenty-five hundred people waking unharvested into a day they would never know had been scheduled otherwise. Saved outright — and nobody has said the word victory since. A stair-post by the river carries one carved word: KEEP.

tiers.name: The Gray Country
tiers.label: the Shadowfell's roads
tiers.text: The world's own shadow — the gray twin of everything, where lost light settles and grief pools like groundwater. Every door they cut, and every door that opens worn, opens there. The cold with a country behind it.

tiers.name: The Gray Country
tiers.label: walked
tiers.text: The world's shadow is a place, and towns and endings cast shadows too. It does not hate — hatred is warmth, and warmth is what it lacks and wants. It leans on the heart the way winter leans on a door; feeling is fuel there, and mourning is the richest fuel of all. Remember everything. Feel nothing you cannot afford.

tiers.name: The Gray Country
tiers.label: the crossed
tiers.text: The company has walked it end to end: its ferry-lights, its keepers, its sorrows housed and feral. The gray always counted heads honestly. It was the only honest thing in the campaign.

tiers.name: The Strait
tiers.label: where the worlds fade together
tiers.text: Not a river with two banks — a fade: two waves precisely opposed leaving a flat calm that is not stillness but war. Ferries cross it with a pale lamp at the bow and a deep-gold lamp at the stern.

tiers.name: The Strait
tiers.label: the failed stitching
tiers.text: The worlds are sewn shut here, and the stitching failed — or was picked — and something has built its house in the gap.

tiers.name: Fundament
tiers.label: a name in the salons
tiers.text: A young polity in the far north-east, out past Sundabar and the last confident maps, toward dead Ascore and the desert's edge. Its name sounds like a promise about floors; its officials go by virtues instead of names, and either that is charming or it is sinister, and nobody can decide.

tiers.name: Fundament
tiers.label: the city of the saved
tiers.text: Real, vast, and kind: a found city righted like a derelict ship, where the Delivered live whole and grateful minus one night apiece. A city found, not founded — and repaired the way swallows build in a cathedral.

tiers.name: Fundament
tiers.label: the doubled city
tiers.text: It stands in both worlds at once, bisecting the seam, lit by two lights that fail to meet. Its doctrine blames the Sharrans, thanks the doors, and is almost right — and no argument is harder to win than an argument against a story that is almost right.

tiers.name: Fundament
tiers.label: the machine
tiers.text: Under the gratitude: advance lists, intake musters, an empty stable sized to one tenant, and a workroom of scores. The city loves its people, and the love is real, and the love is the mechanism.

tiers.name: Ascore
tiers.label: the far anchor
tiers.text: A dead city inland of the far shore, out where the land forgets its names toward the great desert — and at it, the far anchor of the seam. The original, said the way masons say bedrock. It is failing: drift in the harmonics, shear along the fade. If it fails, the strait does not widen politely. It bucks.

tiers.name: Ascore
tiers.label: built around an answer
tiers.text: Delzoun's drowned-in-sand harbor city, ten thousand years quiet, refusing to fall down. At its heart the dwarven work stops at a join, and older, seamless paving begins — the same elder hand as Fundament's bones. The dwarves built their city around a thing that was already old.

tiers.name: Ascore
tiers.label: the city that holds by giving
tiers.text: Its heart is a Mooring — kin to a crystal someone in the company carries — overworked, fed once by a rite of honest music, and holding the tune it was given. What is given, it keeps.

tiers.name: The Receiving Hall
tiers.label: the bottom of the world
tiers.text: A cathedral-nave at the seam's floor where the two countries actually meet: pavement half in each world, ranks of numbered biers, and the Crossing standing at its heart like a sea held upright.

tiers.name: The Receiving Hall
tiers.label: the tenderest crime
tiers.text: Here the Delivered arrive asleep on their feet and are caught, blanketed, and carried up toward the quays — an apparatus of drilled love, run under glad bells, flanked by antechambers whose mirrors hold other places.

tiers.name: The Stable
tiers.label: an emptiness, measured
tiers.text: A vault below even the cathedral: black still water, cradle-ribs like an unbuilt ship, and couplings hanging dead from the unseeable ceiling with their sockets open. Everything in it is sized to one tenant. This is where it will be sad.

tiers.name: The Workroom
tiers.label: the inmost room
tiers.text: An elder chamber opened by three hummed notes: racked black-stone copies, dark mirror-plates, cabling run with a craftsman's love to an empty floor socket — and a worktable where the papers are music.

tiers.name: Jalanthar
tiers.label: a timber town on the Rauvin
tiers.text: A small river town of ferry-trade and woodsmoke, east of Silverymoon. The company once rode within a day of it, in another life.

tiers.name: Jalanthar
tiers.label: the last name on the list
tiers.text: Its people walked through the Crossing asleep — nine hundred and forty biers, a baker still floured from a batch that would burn untended in another world — while a city rang its bells in gratitude.

tiers.name: The Estate
tiers.label: a house in the Hells
tiers.text: A collector's demesne of gravel walks, topiary, and a wine-wall of vintages that are not wine. Nothing in it is employed. Everything in it is owned.

tiers.name: The Estate
tiers.label: the house that fights
tiers.text: The estate is its owner: doors herd, gravel tilts, wounds close as the east wing falls. It was fought, and yielded only to paperwork — and to a very particular fire.

tiers.name: The Bright Country
tiers.label: the first dream's place
tiers.text: Sun-bleached walkways over shallow glittering water, footbridges converging, and a single great tree with worked stone at its root — the brightest place the gray ever shows, returned to like a page held open.

tiers.name: The Bright Country
tiers.label: glimpsed in a mirror
tiers.text: One of the receiving hall's antechamber mirrors holds it in bright morning. Every one of the seven knew it the way you know a room from a dream, and could not place it, and had no time.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the step-through; the stone; the season) unlocks in unwritten chapter XLII.

tiers.name: The Crystal Amulet
tiers.label: a cold inheritance
tiers.text: A small colorless crystal on a cord — the thing Tirig's hand checks for before she is fully awake, without her being able to say why it should come first. Older than any story she has about it.

tiers.name: The Crystal Amulet
tiers.label: the pull north
tiers.text: Held in a closed fist, the crystal leans — a patient, insistent tug, faint as a sleeping pulse, always toward north — and in her fist alone. A geased orc bowed his head to it the way one bows to a superior. It came south with her out of the white, and it points home.

tiers.name: The Heart of Winter's Veil
tiers.label: the stolen Heart
tiers.text: Not a jewel — a kept feeling, old as the Lady's court, distilled through more winters than any line has names for, that held the borderland closed the way a heart holds a body warm. Carried out of the very convoy that was saving it, by a paid thief who does not remember being paid. Returned to its socket, the husk turned like a copied key: the shell remembers the yolk. Nothing sang. The singing has come closer.

tiers.name: The Heart of Winter's Veil
tiers.label: procured; executed; a client's matter
tiers.text: A collector's file names it as merchandise once moved for a client — procured, executed, closed. What kind of client shops for such a thing is a question the file declines to answer.

tiers.name: The Heart of Winter's Veil
tiers.label: the kin stone
tiers.text: At Ascore the Mooring knew it — grown great, or hers grown small, but the same stone. It sings to her now, and she has begun to suspect what a husk is for.
tiers.todo: Tier 5 (what became of the Heart) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: Volcaris
tiers.label: a name out of a mirror
tiers.text: Iratius's blade, which answered to a name he has no memory of learning — Volcaris — and burst into flame at the sound of it. The word came out of a mirror. The fire stayed. And a shadowless bartender has since used the same name for the man who betrayed him.

tiers.name: Volcaris
tiers.label: what the fire runs on
tiers.text: At the devil's true name the blade cracked — a hairline down the fuller, coal-light bleeding through — and spoke one syllable in a voice fifteen years dead: Iratius's name, in his closest squadmate's mouth. Ask what your fire runs on. Ask what everything of his runs on.

tiers.name: Volcaris
tiers.label: that resisted
tiers.text: When the sword-arm was seized, every compelled stroke arrived a half-inch merciful — the twelfth asset paying out its whole hoarded self against its own compulsion. The fire attended the burning of the papers. The fire is particular.

tiers.name: Bayne
tiers.label: a debt in a sack
tiers.text: A blade of pale metal Sov owns and never wears, carried through every mile of this book bundled like a debt — out of a Kelemvorite reliquary in Ormath, in a sack, at night, in these very hands. The Doomguides' priests study it the way an archivist studies a book missing from his own shelves.

tiers.name: Bayne
tiers.label: of the death-god's house
tiers.text: Things with a nose for magic want it badly — it has had to be smothered like a fevered child while blind things hunted the sound of it. What the death-god's house forged it for, the house is not saying.

tiers.name: A Bottle from the Wall
tiers.label: not wine
tiers.text: One vintage from a collector's wall: honey-and-morning, festival-colored, shining. The gray was never in the bottle; the gray is what a place is, after the bottle.

tiers.name: The Shining Bottle
tiers.label: gratis; goodwill toward the yielding
tiers.text: Bought back at embarrassment prices with the pact-papers, wrapped, unopened. The company knows who it is for, and is not telling yet.

tiers.name: The Shining Bottle
tiers.label: concentrated childhood
tiers.text: In the desert a blind miner of magic reached for the pack it rode in before anything else the company carried. Whatever a childhood weighs, it shines brighter than swords.
tiers.todo: Tier 4 (the delivery) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIV+.

tiers.name: A Soul Coin
tiers.label: kept in a snuffbox
tiers.text: A coin of the Hells' currency, displayed at a collector's table with the pride of a completed set. He only ever called them his brothers.

tiers.name: The Doorknocker Coin
tiers.label: eleven souls, carried
tiers.text: Iratius's squad — eleven of the twelve — bound in one coin and carried now over his heart. The papers burned. The coin did not. What is owed to it has no line in any ledger yet.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the release) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLV+.

tiers.name: The Obsidian Knife
tiers.label: worked loose from a jaw
tiers.text: A blade of black glass worked free from a dead horror's jaw as it fell — volcanic-sharp, strangely balanced, and kept, because Corvyn keeps what the dark gives him.

tiers.name: The Obsidian Knife
tiers.label: the key to the kept
tiers.text: One of a pair, it turns out — and its edge does to standing glass what edges should not do. What it opens is not doors but keepings; it has been measured by more than one pair of eyes that understood it instantly.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (handed back; the belt at morning) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIV+.

tiers.name: The Scales Shield
tiers.label: six-sided, blazoned
tiers.text: Sov's shield, painted with a set of scales. It has stood at doors as ward and accusation both, and been taken — in one particular house — as a compliment.

tiers.name: The Resonance Bowl
tiers.label: an old bard's instrument
tiers.text: Aelendir's bowl of resonant metal, played with wand and breath. It is older than his story about it, which is true of him generally.

tiers.name: The Resonance Bowl
tiers.label: that was there
tiers.text: A dissonance rang in it at Triboar like an answer to a question no one had asked yet. Where it has been played before matters more than where it will be played next.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the ring of hands) unlocks at door07.

tiers.name: The Conserved Sheet
tiers.label: one page, mended with reverence
tiers.text: Centuries old, ink browned, folds mended by a conservator's hand: the tune, entire, right way round, in an elegant unhurried elvish hand the company has seen on requisitions and ledger-lines.

tiers.name: Aelendir's Notation
tiers.label: stolen first
tiers.text: His own hand, four hundred years old, looted from a country whose name he lost with everything else — and now folded inside his coat, over his heart, where Saeron keeps a key. She stole it first.

tiers.name: The Silent Ledger
tiers.label: a book that says nothing
tiers.text: A hidden ledger of Hyuth's assurance deals, spoken of before it was ever seen and seized from a warded study — written in a cipher that resists every honest key. Whoever kept it trusted no one, including the future.

tiers.name: The Silent Ledger
tiers.label: opened at last
tiers.text: Opened at last — not whole, but walking. The order's accounts, and the order never once writes its own name. What it writes is a calendar: the veil-thin nights entered like quarter-days in a countinghouse. Highharvestide — entered, and reconciled. The Feast of the Moon — entered, and pending. Cargo: as the last intake, in full, less the error.

tiers.name: The Silent Ledger
tiers.label: the counterparty
tiers.text: Threaded through the accounts, season upon season, a counterparty — payments in, product out — signed with a true name in a fiend's hand, old-fashioned and vain of its flourishes. Not the name given on the moor. Either the web has two spiders, or one spider wears two names.

tiers.name: The Ink on Her Arm
tiers.label: written standing
tiers.text: Block capitals on the Lord Protector's forearm, written at the arch's head while it took the last of the rescued — unhurried, like a woman labeling a crate — and rolled under the vambrace.

tiers.name: The Transcription
tiers.label: copied twice and washed
tiers.text: In Fundament she found it on her own arm with no memory of writing it, copied it twice, and washed it off — a Lord Protector cannot be seen wearing madness on her arm — and carried the sheet folded, like a wound she could not locate.

tiers.name: The Testament
tiers.label: the death-rite, recited
tiers.text: Her private vow since twenty-two: written only when death stands certain in the doorway. Seven witnesses gave it back to her word for word — no rescue, no regret, by my own choice, knowing — and its existence proves a lie built exactly the size of her death.

tiers.name: The Antechamber Mirrors
tiers.label: instruments of a finer make
tiers.text: Tall frames of elder pale stone in the receiving hall's flanking bays — between the Sharran mirrors the company broke and the honest arch at Moongleam, some third thing — each holding, in reflection, somewhere else: a rain-dark street, a harbor, a moor-rise, a bright morning.

tiers.name: The Doors
tiers.label: trials that open inward
tiers.text: Each of the seven carries a burden that is also a threshold. When a burden heightens past bearing, its door opens — a thin place, a trial, and kin that come calling.

tiers.name: The Doors
tiers.label: seven, addressed by name
tiers.text: There are seven doors, six standing in the country ahead — each belonging to one keeper, bought with what they carried out of the gray, answerable by nobody else. The seventh is not missing; it waits deeper in the book, for reasons the book will earn. Behind every door is something that was kept — not hidden; kept.

tiers.name: The Doors
tiers.label: the pattern
tiers.text: Damage never wins a door. The keeper must do the opposite of what the burden demands — choose when choosing is impossible, reach when reaching is the wound. The fight is the lock; the vision is what opens.

tiers.name: The Doors
tiers.label: the seventh
tiers.text: The Spring Door — first of all of them, and opened last. Its keeper stood outside the bargain the others were inside, which is why his opens differently, and why it has sound.
tiers.todo: Tier 5 (the closings) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: The Remembrances
tiers.label: silent films in the gray
tiers.text: Scenes of a life the gray grants at the doors: memories walked through rather than watched, silent as deep water. Footprints refused, faces unfound — and the words on the woman's lips readable, because some of what she was, the watchers carry.

tiers.name: The Remembrances
tiers.label: whose life
tiers.text: They are one woman's keeping, played back: the girl at the grave, the hearth, the market, the wall of best days. And in the Remembrance of Euphoria, for the first time, there is sound — the song itself, whole verses, water-far — because joy keeps everything, including the hearing.

tiers.name: The Remembrances
tiers.label: the mosaic
tiers.text: Assembled in the order the doors chose, they build an argument: ambivalence, loneliness, melancholy, euphoria, wrath, empathy — the emotional inventory of someone who paid herself away. The seventh plays with full sound, because its witness was really there.

tiers.name: The Sorrowsworn
tiers.label: grief with a body
tiers.text: Small wretched shapes knit from the shed grief and fright of a dying town — hunched things that weep and bite, pale things that want only to be held and would drown you holding back. Feelings given bodies before their time. The name, learned much later: Sorrowsworn.

tiers.name: The Sorrowsworn
tiers.label: housed and feral
tiers.text: An emotion carried willingly is housed — stable, symbiotic, a burden that steadies its bearer. An emotion orphaned from its person curdles feral. The five feral kinds are orphans, every one.
tiers.todo: Unlocks in Appendix A (unwritten): the housed/feral taxonomy as Consensus field documentation.

tiers.name: The Sorrowsworn
tiers.label: the sworn
tiers.text: Some ferals were caught and sworn into service as the gray's own psychopomps — sorrow put to work carrying sorrow. The first ferals were ash of an ascension, which means the corps eternally cleans up its own founding.
tiers.todo: Unlocks in Appendix A / unwritten chapters XLIII+: the sworn corps and the ash of the founding.

tiers.name: The Unmoored
tiers.label: bodies rewritten
tiers.text: Beasts and worse, remade into wrongness by the black ichor: wrong eyes, wrong movement, right teeth. Loosed from their own natures — a corruption that does not so much kill as rewrite.

tiers.name: The Unmoored
tiers.label: the ichor line
tiers.text: Where the worlds chafe, an ichor gets into living things and edits them — a bear, a stag, wolves with black-threaded gums, birds that come back flying wrong. The line runs from the seams: wherever the border stands, the forest starts coming over.

tiers.name: The Harvest
tiers.label: an order in a dead woman's hand
tiers.text: Four words in a firm, unhurried script, recovered from a severed grip in a ransacked camp: Prepare for Harvest. Signed with a virtue for a name. What is being harvested, and by whom, and why a murder was its preparation, the order does not say.

tiers.name: The Harvest
tiers.label: the taking
tiers.text: The rite's output: black glass rising along the seams of a town on the year's oldest turning-day, taking people whole and standing. The priests did not conduct it; they attended it. You cannot stop a season.

tiers.name: The Harvest
tiers.label: one step of many
tiers.text: Triboar was neither first nor last: there are advance lists, seasons deep, and the taken arrive elsewhere whole — minus each carrier's memory of the carrying. The purpose of the gathering is stabilization; of what, the lists decline to say.

tiers.name: The Deliverance
tiers.label: the doctrine of the saved
tiers.text: Fundament's founding story: towns doomed by the Sharrans' workings, saved through the doors that mercy prepared, kept in gratitude. It is told with bells, flowers, and complete sincerity.

tiers.name: The Deliverance
tiers.label: almost right
tiers.text: The shrine reliefs show mirror-faced Sharrans reaching after ascending wagons and falling short. The doctrine's every detail is checkable, and checks out, and is a lie built out of true parts — and no argument is harder to win than an argument against a story that is almost right.

tiers.name: The Deliverance
tiers.label: the work
tiers.text: Seen from the intake floor: advance lists, glad bells, drilled tenderness, a town received asleep and carried up to wake saved. The love is real. The love is the mechanism.

tiers.name: The Session
tiers.label: how Fundament is handled
tiers.text: Six offices — Diplomat, Seeker, Priest, Warrior, Enforcer, Oracle — that do not rule; ruling is a claim. They handle: outside, unknown, kept, far, near, and what is coming. Unanimity only. Patient people.

tiers.name: The Session
tiers.label: the table and the gallery
tiers.text: Votes are spoken for the office, liturgy is debated like ordnance, Avernus sends invoices, and the traffic of the room bends around a chair no one sits in.

tiers.name: The Seventh Chair
tiers.label: an absence at the head
tiers.text: Empty at the table's head, and the room bends around it. One member bows to it when he believes himself unwatched. Questions about it have a single answer, which is not given.

tiers.name: The Seventh Chair
tiers.label: whose
tiers.text: The founders considered a stalled table the point — but the chair is not a founder's memorial. It is kept for someone, by instruction, and the instruction is obeyed with reverence.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the occupant) unlocks at door07 and unwritten chapters XLIII+.

tiers.name: The Twelve
tiers.label: Triboar's sworn wardens
tiers.text: The Lord Protector's picked dozen: rotations, keys, audits. A town's trust, in twelve coats.

tiers.name: The Twelve
tiers.label: minus one, then minus more
tiers.text: The rotations were tampered with, the tampering burned, and the burner wore an inquisitor's sash. Trust, it turns out, was the first thing harvested.

tiers.name: The Harpers
tiers.label: those who harp and hope
tiers.text: The North's quiet network of couriers, wardens, and watchers, who take in the washed-up and move the un-movable. Their birds arrive iced and furious.

tiers.name: The Harpers
tiers.label: keepers of the aftermath
tiers.text: They hold Moongleam's forty, ward a bound squire, decode what cannot be read, and lose exactly one boy east of Silverymoon — and enter the loss honestly.

tiers.name: The Glass
tiers.label: what rises
tiers.text: Black, slow, and certain: a substance that rises along seams and takes what it touches — takes, not kills. Where it has been, places are quieter than empty.

tiers.name: The Glass
tiers.label: the carrying
tiers.text: What the glass takes arrives elsewhere, whole, minus the night of the taking. It is a door pretending to be a disaster — or a disaster employed as a door.

tiers.name: The Glass
tiers.label: the shearing toll
tiers.text: The door cuts. That is what the door is for. It shears loose what you are carrying — the night of you — and keeps it somewhere in the toll. It cannot cut what something else is holding for you.

tiers.name: The Black Stones
tiers.label: anchors of wrongness
tiers.text: Black stones worked with etched runes, found where the world wears thinnest — levitating, light-bending, sound-muffling, wrong. Around such stones things go wrong the way milk goes wrong, and the dead are not permitted to stay finished.

tiers.name: The Black Stones
tiers.label: copies
tiers.text: They are duplicates of something older — anchors made without feeling, that take instead of hold. The original work moored the planes safely apart; the copies haul them together like a fouled mooring hauls a ship onto rocks.

tiers.name: The Moorings
tiers.label: what holds by giving
tiers.text: The originals are emotion-crystals: they hold feeling, hold the planes riding apart, and have been drawing on their own reserves for ten thousand years — because everyone takes and nobody has ever put anything back in. Except once. What is given, they keep.

tiers.name: Three Wrong Notes
tiers.label: a tune nobody taught them
tiers.text: A melodic scrap the whole company knows without having learned: three notes, slightly wrong, that feel like the start of something none of them can finish.

tiers.name: The Tune
tiers.label: the fellowship's song
tiers.text: It is old — older than any of their lives should reach — and it belongs to a fellowship glimpsed in the Remembrances: a rope-line, a wall, a ring of hands. It is the kindest thing one of them knows.

tiers.name: The Tune
tiers.label: that stone remembers
tiers.text: Played honestly into the Mooring of Ascore, it was kept — the stone holds the tune. Doors of the elder work open to it. It is a key, and it was a gift first.

tiers.name: The Tune
tiers.label: taken apart
tiers.text: In the enemy's workroom it lies unraveled: every phrase inverted, every resolution refused, arranged to cut. What the whole song is for — right way round — no page in that room says.

tiers.name: The Song of Unraveling
tiers.label: a butcher's diagram of a beloved animal
tiers.text: The tune run backward against itself, annotated in the grammar of the devout: sung thus at the threshold; the unbinding descends here; the choir holds the lattice while the operator ascends. What it would cut, and from whom, and to what end, the pages do not say.

tiers.name: Silver Fire
tiers.label: the North's clean burn
tiers.text: A radiance in the Silverhand blood that burns corruption out of what it touches. It is one of the only ways anyone has ever closed a shadow crossing.

tiers.name: Silver Fire
tiers.label: the echo
tiers.text: The company has seen the same clean burning once before, in a place and a person no doctrine accounts for — and the resemblance is not a coincidence. It is an inheritance.

tiers.name: In Transit
tiers.label: a column that should not exist
tiers.text: Fundament's ledgers carry souls neither arrived nor lost: in transit — some for nine years. Either the column is a lie, or there is a place between the shores, and it has a waiting room.

tiers.name: The In-Transit Column
tiers.label: being emptied
tiers.text: The company has a name from it now, and a stated intention, and a Lord Protector who calls it the correct use of paperwork.
tiers.todo: Tier 3 (the waiting room; the recoveries) unlocks in unwritten chapters XLIII–XLIV.
